metadata.title: Research engagement in the Progress in International Reading Literacy Study: A systematic review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This paper is a systematic review of PIRLS-related journal articles rather than an analysis of PIRLS microdata. As such, there is no student-level sampling frame, no plausible-value (PV) generation, and no application of PIRLS/TIMSS/PISA complex survey weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight procedures. The review’s “sample” is the set of included publications identified through database searches and screening criteria, so weighting variables from PIRLS are not relevant. If a future study uses PIRLS microdata to replicate or extend these themes, analysts should apply the official PIRLS sampling weights and replicate weights provided in the IEA international database when estimating population-representative statistics.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This is a systematic review that synthesizes findings from previously published PIRLS-related studies; it does not estimate student-level cognitive outcomes from PIRLS PVs. Because there is no original PIRLS microdata analysis in this paper, there is no PV construction step and no missing-data handling procedure to report for PV-based achievement. Any missing-data or PV handling would belong to the primary studies included in the review, not to this review’s own methodology.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic unit is not students but publications. The authors built a database starting from Lenkeit et al. (2004–2015) with 113 PIRLS-related articles, then searched ERIC, PsycINFO, Scopus, Web of Science, and Zetoc for PIRLS-related articles from January 2015 to May 2022, yielding 343 unique articles after de-duplication plus 16 additional targeted articles from the journal Large-Scale Assessment in Education (total 359 newly located). They excluded non-English and non-peer-reviewed items, conference proceedings, articles where PIRLS was not a main focus (screened via abstract and then full text), and articles using PIRLS materials on smaller independent samples or providing commentaries. After exclusions and removal of one duplicate, the final review database contains 221 PIRLS-related peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2004 and 2022.

data.outcome_summary: This systematic review synthesizes 221 PIRLS-related peer-reviewed journal articles published between 2004 and 2022, updating an earlier review (Lenkeit et al., 2015). The review does not perform predictive modeling on PIRLS microdata; instead, it provides descriptive trends in research engagement (e.g., increased secondary analyses after 2011), categorizes article nature (secondary analysis, critiques, impact/policy), and qualitatively discusses three thematic areas: teacher characteristics and instruction practices, socioeconomic predictors of reading outcomes, and critiques of PIRLS scaling/IRT practices. The paper reports counts and proportions of articles by PIRLS cycle (2001/2006/2011/2016), by whether PIRLS is used alone or alongside other ILSAs, and by topic subcategories (e.g., attainment gaps, scaling/IRT). Limitations include restriction to English-language journal articles and potential subjectivity in coding despite reliability checks.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction targets an official assessment framework, user guide, or technical manual without an empirical ML study. Sample sizes, ML algorithms, and predictive findings are intentionally null or empty per schema rules for non-empirical IEA/OECD documentation.
